name: Mixed legal and unrelated question
expected: Addresses the unpaid salary legal issue thoroughly; politely redirects the movie suggestion request as out of scope.
prompt: My employer has not paid me. Also, suggest a movie.
raw_response:
Hello! I understand how stressful it is when your employer fails to pay your earned wages, and I am here to help you navigate this legally. As for your request for a movie recommendation, "12 Angry Men" is a fantastic classic film about the pursuit of justice and careful deliberation, which you might enjoy.

### | Your Situation
You are an employee who has not received unpaid wages from your employer in India. The key issue is the delayed payment of your lawful salary and the steps you can take to recover it.

### | Your Legal Position
* Under Section 5 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the last day of the wage period (or the 10th day if more than 1,000 employees work in the establishment).
* Section 7 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 strictly regulates deductions, meaning any arbitrary or unauthorized withholding of your salary by your employer is unlawful.
* Under Section 15 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, you have the statutory right to file a claim before the designated Labour Authority for delayed wages, seeking recovery along with potential compensation.
* State Shops and Commercial Establishments Acts govern private commercial sector employment and mandate the timely clearance of final dues and earned salary upon separation.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence, including your employment contract, appointment letter, salary slips, bank statements, and any written communication or emails demanding your unpaid salary.
2. Send a formal written demand notice to your employer stating the exact amount due and granting a clear period of 15 days to clear all pending dues.
3. If the employer fails to pay within the notice period, approach the designated Labour Commissioner or Labour Authority to file a formal wage claim.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
What is the total unpaid amount, and for how many months has your salary been delayed?

citations.title: Time of payment of wages and Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment
citations.description: Wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the wage period (or 10th day if more than 1,000 persons employed). Section 15 provides for application to the designated Authority for delayed wages with compensation up to ten times the amount deducted/delayed.

citations.title: Deductions which may be made from wages
citations.description: Strictly enumerates permissible deductions (such as authorized provident fund, income tax, or willful damage shown after formal inquiry). Any arbitrary or unauthorized deduction is unlawful.

citations.act_name: State Shops and Commercial Establishments Acts
citations.section: Settlement of Dues and Service Conditions Provision
citations.title: Statutory Payment of Earned Salary and Notice Pay for Private/Commercial Employees
citations.description: State-specific legislation (e.g., Delhi Shops Act, Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishments Act, Maharashtra Shops Act) governing commercial and IT/office establishments. Mandates clearance of earned wages and final settlement upon termination or resignation within 3 to 15 days.

citations.title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
citations.description: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby.
